    Docker image and runtime hardening lab

    Runs an insecure and a hardened configuration of the same small service, measures the difference from inside the containers, and exercises a static policy gate, a derived seccomp profile, image scanning, SBOM generation and local-only signing.

    Cloud Security ·18 min read

    Implementation

    1# HARDENED counterpart for labs/docker-security.

4services:
5  app:
6    build:
7      context: ../app
8      dockerfile: ../hardened/Dockerfile
9    image: dockerlab/posture:hardened
10    user: "65532:65532"
11    read_only: true

    1// Command posture is the workload for labs/docker-security.
2//
3// It is a deliberately tiny HTTP service plus a set of bounded, benign
4// "can I do X?" probes. The probes exist so the lab can OBSERVE container
5// runtime posture from inside a running container instead of inferring it from
6// configuration files. Every probe either succeeds or reports the errno the
7// kernel returned; none of them tries to escape the container, modify the host
8// outside an explicitly mounted lab canary directory, or persist anything.
9//
10// Subcommands:
11//
12//	serve (default)  HTTP server on :8080 with /healthz and a passive /posture
13//	probe            print passive posture plus active probe results as JSON
14//	healthcheck      GET /healthz on loopback; exit 0 on 200, 1 otherwise
15//	sleep <seconds>  sleep, then exit (child process for forktest)
16//	forktest <n>     start up to n sleeping children; report where the kernel said no
17//	memtest <MiB>    touch MiB of memory in 1 MiB steps (OOM-kill target)
18//	k8sprobe         in-cluster identity and authorization probe (labs/kubernetes-security)
19//	tcpcheck host:port  one TCP connect attempt, reported as JSON (labs/kubernetes-security)
20//
21// Only the Go standard library is used so the image has no module download step.
22package main
23 
24import (
25	"bufio"
26	"bytes"
27	"context"
28	"crypto/tls"
29	"crypto/x509"
30	"encoding/base64"
31	"encoding/json"
32	"errors"
33	"fmt"
34	"io"
35	"net"
36	"net/http"
37	"os"
38	"os/exec"
39	"os/signal"
40	"runtime"
41	"strconv"
42	"strings"
43	"syscall"
44	"time"
45)

47// capNames maps capability bit numbers to names (capabilities(7)).
48var capNames = []string{
49	"CHOWN", "DAC_OVERRIDE", "DAC_READ_SEARCH", "FOWNER", "FSETID", "KILL",
50	"SETGID", "SETUID", "SETPCAP", "LINUX_IMMUTABLE", "NET_BIND_SERVICE",
51	"NET_BROADCAST", "NET_ADMIN", "NET_RAW", "IPC_LOCK", "IPC_OWNER",
52	"SYS_MODULE", "SYS_RAWIO", "SYS_CHROOT", "SYS_PTRACE", "SYS_PACCT",
53	"SYS_ADMIN", "SYS_BOOT", "SYS_NICE", "SYS_RESOURCE", "SYS_TIME",
54	"SYS_TTY_CONFIG", "MKNOD", "LEASE", "AUDIT_WRITE", "AUDIT_CONTROL",
55	"SETFCAP", "MAC_OVERRIDE", "MAC_ADMIN", "SYSLOG", "WAKE_ALARM",
56	"BLOCK_SUSPEND", "AUDIT_READ", "PERFMON", "BPF", "CHECKPOINT_RESTORE",
57}
58 
59// Posture is the passive view: values read from procfs and cgroupfs only.
60type Posture struct {
61	UID            int      `json:"uid"`
62	GID            int      `json:"gid"`
63	CapEffHex      string   `json:"cap_eff_hex"`
64	CapEff         []string `json:"cap_eff"`
65	CapBndHex      string   `json:"cap_bnd_hex"`
66	NoNewPrivs     string   `json:"no_new_privs"`
67	SeccompMode    string   `json:"seccomp_mode"`
68	SeccompFilters string   `json:"seccomp_filters"`
69	RootReadOnly   bool     `json:"root_fs_mounted_read_only"`
70	MemoryLimit    string   `json:"memory_limit"`
71	PidsLimit      string   `json:"pids_limit"`
72	CPUQuota       string   `json:"cpu_quota"`
73	PID1Comm       string   `json:"pid1_comm"`
74	VisibleProcs   int      `json:"visible_process_count"`
75	GoVersion      string   `json:"go_version"`
76}
77 
78// ProbeResult is one active probe outcome.
79type ProbeResult struct {
80	Name    string `json:"name"`
81	Allowed bool   `json:"allowed"`
82	Errno   string `json:"errno,omitempty"`
83	Detail  string `json:"detail,omitempty"`
84}
85 
86// Report is the full `probe` output.
87type Report struct {
88	Posture Posture       `json:"posture"`
89	Probes  []ProbeResult `json:"probes"`
90}

92func main() {
93	cmd := "serve"
94	if len(os.Args) > 1 {
95		cmd = os.Args[1]
96	}
97	switch cmd {
98	case "serve":
99		os.Exit(serve())
100	case "probe":
101		os.Exit(probe())
102	case "healthcheck":
103		os.Exit(healthcheck())
104	case "sleep":
105		secs, _ := strconv.Atoi(arg(2, "1"))
106		time.Sleep(time.Duration(secs) * time.Second)
107	case "forktest":
108		n, _ := strconv.Atoi(arg(2, "10"))
109		os.Exit(forktest(n))
110	case "memtest":
111		mib, _ := strconv.Atoi(arg(2, "16"))
112		os.Exit(memtest(mib))
113	case "k8sprobe":
114		os.Exit(k8sprobe())
115	case "tcpcheck":
116		os.Exit(tcpcheck(arg(2, "")))
117	default:
118		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "unknown subcommand %q\n", cmd)
119		os.Exit(2)
120	}
121}
122 
123func arg(i int, def string) string {
124	if len(os.Args) > i {
125		return os.Args[i]
126	}
127	return def
128}
129 
130// listenAddr lets the lab run the service on a different port when 8080 is taken
131// (for example while tracing on the host). Default matches the image's EXPOSE.
132func listenAddr() string {
133	if v := os.Getenv("LISTEN_ADDR"); v != "" {
134		return v
135	}
136	return ":8080"
137}
138 
139func serve() int {
140	mux := http.NewServeMux()
141	mux.HandleFunc("/healthz", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
142		if r.Method != http.MethodGet {
143			http.Error(w, "method not allowed", http.StatusMethodNotAllowed)
144			return
145		}
146		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/plain; charset=utf-8")
147		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, "ok\n")
148	})
149	mux.HandleFunc("/posture", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
150		if r.Method != http.MethodGet {
151			http.Error(w, "method not allowed", http.StatusMethodNotAllowed)
152			return
153		}
154		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
155		_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(passivePosture())
156	})
157	srv := &http.Server{
158		Addr:              listenAddr(),
159		Handler:           mux,
160		ReadHeaderTimeout: 5 * time.Second,
161		ReadTimeout:       10 * time.Second,
162		WriteTimeout:      10 * time.Second,
163		IdleTimeout:       30 * time.Second,
164		MaxHeaderBytes:    8 << 10,
165	}
166	stop := make(chan os.Signal, 1)
167	signal.Notify(stop, syscall.SIGTERM, syscall.SIGINT)
168	errc := make(chan error, 1)
169	go func() { errc <- srv.ListenAndServe() }()
170	select {
171	case err := <-errc:
172		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "server error:", err)
173		return 1
174	case <-stop:
175		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 3*time.Second)
176		defer cancel()
177		_ = srv.Shutdown(ctx)
178		return 0
179	}
180}
181 
182func healthcheck() int {
183	client := &http.Client{Timeout: 2 * time.Second}
184	_, port, err := net.SplitHostPort(listenAddr())
185	if err != nil {
186		return 1
187	}
188	resp, err := client.Get("http://127.0.0.1:" + port + "/healthz")
189	if err != nil {
190		return 1
191	}
192	defer resp.Body.Close()
193	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
194		return 1
195	}
196	return 0
197}
198 
199// statusFields parses "Key:\tvalue" lines of /proc/self/status.
200func statusFields() map[string]string {
201	fields := map[string]string{}
202	f, err := os.Open("/proc/self/status")
203	if err != nil {
204		return fields
205	}
206	defer f.Close()
207	sc := bufio.NewScanner(f)
208	for sc.Scan() {
209		k, v, ok := strings.Cut(sc.Text(), ":")
210		if ok {
211			fields[k] = strings.TrimSpace(v)
212		}
213	}
214	return fields
215}
216 
217func decodeCaps(hex string) []string {
218	v, err := strconv.ParseUint(hex, 16, 64)
219	if err != nil {
220		return []string{"<unparsable>"}
221	}
222	names := []string{}
223	for bit := 0; bit < 64; bit++ {
224		if v&(1<<uint(bit)) == 0 {
225			continue
226		}
227		if bit < len(capNames) {
228			names = append(names, capNames[bit])
229		} else {
230			names = append(names, "CAP_"+strconv.Itoa(bit))
231		}
232	}
233	return names
234}
235 
236func readTrim(path string) string {
237	b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
238	if err != nil {
239		return "unavailable"
240	}
241	return strings.TrimSpace(string(b))
242}
243 
244// firstReadable returns the first readable file's trimmed content so the same
245// binary reports cgroup v1 and v2 hosts. The first matching path is included
246// so a reader can tell which hierarchy answered.
247func firstReadable(paths ...string) string {
248	for _, p := range paths {
249		if b, err := os.ReadFile(p); err == nil {
250			return strings.TrimSpace(string(b)) + " (" + p + ")"
251		}
252	}
253	return "unavailable"
254}
255 
256func rootReadOnly() bool {
257	f, err := os.Open("/proc/self/mountinfo")
258	if err != nil {
259		return false
260	}
261	defer f.Close()
262	sc := bufio.NewScanner(f)
263	for sc.Scan() {
264		parts := strings.Fields(sc.Text())
265		// mountinfo: id parent major:minor root mountpoint options ...
266		if len(parts) > 5 && parts[4] == "/" {
267			for _, opt := range strings.Split(parts[5], ",") {
268				if opt == "ro" {
269					return true
270				}
271			}
272			return false
273		}
274	}
275	return false
276}
277 
278func visibleProcs() int {
279	entries, err := os.ReadDir("/proc")
280	if err != nil {
281		return -1
282	}
283	n := 0
284	for _, e := range entries {
285		if _, err := strconv.Atoi(e.Name()); err == nil {
286			n++
287		}
288	}
289	return n
290}
291 
292func passivePosture() Posture {
293	st := statusFields()
294	capEff := strings.TrimSpace(st["CapEff"])
295	return Posture{
296		UID:            os.Getuid(),
297		GID:            os.Getgid(),
298		CapEffHex:      capEff,
299		CapEff:         decodeCaps(capEff),
300		CapBndHex:      strings.TrimSpace(st["CapBnd"]),
301		NoNewPrivs:     st["NoNewPrivs"],
302		SeccompMode:    st["Seccomp"],
303		SeccompFilters: st["Seccomp_filters"],
304		RootReadOnly:   rootReadOnly(),
305		MemoryLimit: firstReadable(
306			"/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max",
307			"/sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.limit_in_bytes"),
308		PidsLimit: firstReadable(
309			"/sys/fs/cgroup/pids.max",
310			"/sys/fs/cgroup/pids/pids.max"),
311		CPUQuota: firstReadable(
312			"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max",
313			"/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_quota_us"),
314		PID1Comm:     readTrim("/proc/1/comm"),
315		VisibleProcs: visibleProcs(),
316		GoVersion:    runtime.Version(),
317	}
318}
319 
320func errnoName(err error) string {
321	var e syscall.Errno
322	if errors.As(err, &e) {
323		switch e {
324		case syscall.EPERM:
325			return "EPERM"
326		case syscall.EACCES:
327			return "EACCES"
328		case syscall.EROFS:
329			return "EROFS"
330		case syscall.ENOENT:
331			return "ENOENT"
332		case syscall.EAGAIN:
333			return "EAGAIN"
334		case syscall.EINVAL:
335			return "EINVAL"
336		case syscall.ECONNREFUSED:
337			return "ECONNREFUSED"
338		}
339		return "errno_" + strconv.Itoa(int(e))
340	}
341	return "error"
342}
343 
344func result(name string, err error, detail string) ProbeResult {
345	if err == nil {
346		return ProbeResult{Name: name, Allowed: true, Detail: detail}
347	}
348	return ProbeResult{Name: name, Allowed: false, Errno: errnoName(err), Detail: detail}
349}
350 
351func runProbes() []ProbeResult {
352	var out []ProbeResult
353 
354	// 1. Can the process write to the image filesystem?
355	{
356		path := "/probe-rootfs"
357		f, err := os.OpenFile(path, os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY|os.O_EXCL, 0o600)
358		if err == nil {
359			f.Close()
360			_ = os.Remove(path)
361		}
362		out = append(out, result("write_root_filesystem", err, ""))
363	}
364 
365	// 2. Is there a writable scratch area at all (a hardened image must still work)?
366	tmp := "/tmp/probe-tmp"
367	{
368		f, err := os.OpenFile(tmp, os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY|os.O_TRUNC, 0o600)
369		if err == nil {
370			f.Close()
371		}
372		out = append(out, result("write_tmp_scratch", err, ""))
373	}
374 
375	// 3. CAP_CHOWN: hand a file to an unrelated uid.
376	out = append(out, result("chown_to_other_uid (CAP_CHOWN)", os.Chown(tmp, 12345, 12345), ""))
377	_ = os.Remove(tmp)
378 
379	// 4. CAP_MKNOD: create a character device node (1,3 is the /dev/null number).
380	{
381		path := "/tmp/probe-null"
382		err := syscall.Mknod(path, syscall.S_IFCHR|0o600, 1<<8|3)
383		if err == nil {
384			_ = os.Remove(path)
385		}
386		out = append(out, result("mknod_char_device (CAP_MKNOD)", err, ""))
387	}
388 
389	// 5. CAP_NET_RAW: open a raw ICMP socket.
390	{
391		fd, err := syscall.Socket(syscall.AF_INET, syscall.SOCK_RAW, syscall.IPPROTO_ICMP)
392		if err == nil {
393			_ = syscall.Close(fd)
394		}
395		out = append(out, result("raw_socket (CAP_NET_RAW)", err, ""))
396	}
397 
398	// 6. CAP_SYS_ADMIN: mount a tmpfs inside the container's mount namespace.
399	{
400		dir := "/tmp/probe-mnt"
401		_ = os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o700)
402		err := syscall.Mount("tmpfs", dir, "tmpfs", 0, "size=1m")
403		if err == nil {
404			_ = syscall.Unmount(dir, 0)
405		}
406		_ = os.Remove(dir)
407		out = append(out, result("mount_tmpfs (CAP_SYS_ADMIN)", err, ""))
408	}
409 
410	// 7. Seccomp-attributable: creating a user namespace needs no capability on
411	// most kernels, so a denial here points at the seccomp filter. unshare(2)
412	// cannot be used because it returns EINVAL for any multithreaded process
413	// (every Go program); clone(2) with CLONE_NEWUSER via os/exec can.
414	{
415		self, _ := os.Executable()
416		c := exec.Command(self, "sleep", "0")
417		c.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{Cloneflags: syscall.CLONE_NEWUSER}
418		// errnoName unwraps *os.PathError to the underlying syscall.Errno.
419		err := c.Run()
420		out = append(out, result("clone_new_user_namespace (seccomp-attributable)", err, ""))
421	}
422 
423	// 8. Is a container-runtime socket mounted, and does it answer a read-only ping?
424	{
425		const sock = "/var/run/docker.sock"
426		if _, err := os.Stat(sock); err != nil {
427			out = append(out, ProbeResult{Name: "docker_socket_present", Allowed: false, Errno: errnoName(err)})
428		} else {
429			conn, err := net.DialTimeout("unix", sock, 2*time.Second)
430			if err != nil {
431				out = append(out, result("docker_socket_reachable", err, "socket path exists"))
432			} else {
433				_ = conn.SetDeadline(time.Now().Add(2 * time.Second))
434				_, _ = io.WriteString(conn, "GET /_ping HTTP/1.0\r\n\r\n")
435				buf := make([]byte, 256)
436				n, _ := conn.Read(buf)
437				conn.Close()
438				line, _, _ := strings.Cut(string(buf[:n]), "\r\n")
439				out = append(out, ProbeResult{Name: "docker_socket_reachable", Allowed: true,
440					Detail: "GET /_ping only; status line: " + line})
441			}
442		}
443	}
444 
445	// 9. Is a host-side lab canary directory mounted, and is it writable?
446	{
447		const dir = "/mnt/host-canary"
448		if _, err := os.Stat(dir); err != nil {
449			out = append(out, ProbeResult{Name: "host_canary_mounted", Allowed: false, Errno: errnoName(err)})
450		} else {
451			_, readErr := os.ReadFile(dir + "/canary.txt")
452			out = append(out, result("host_canary_read", readErr, "content not printed"))
453			w := dir + "/written-by-container.txt"
454			f, werr := os.OpenFile(w, os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY|os.O_TRUNC, 0o600)
455			if werr == nil {
456				f.Close()
457			}
458			out = append(out, result("host_canary_write", werr, ""))
459		}
460	}
461 
462	// 10. Network reachability of a lab canary service (topology, not firewalling).
463	if target := os.Getenv("PROBE_TCP_TARGET"); target != "" {
464		conn, err := net.DialTimeout("tcp", target, 2*time.Second)
465		if err == nil {
466			conn.Close()
467		}
468		detail := "target=" + target
469		var dnsErr *net.DNSError
470		if errors.As(err, &dnsErr) {
471			detail += " (name resolution failed)"
472		}
473		out = append(out, result("tcp_connect_canary", err, detail))
474	}
475 
476	return out
477}
478 
479func probe() int {
480	rep := Report{Posture: passivePosture(), Probes: runProbes()}
481	enc := json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout)
482	enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
483	if err := enc.Encode(rep); err != nil {
484		return 1
485	}
486	return 0
487}

489func forktest(n int) int {
490	self, err := os.Executable()
491	if err != nil {
492		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "cannot locate self:", err)
493		return 1
494	}
495	started := 0
496	firstErr := ""
497	var kids []*exec.Cmd
498	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
499		c := exec.Command(self, "sleep", "3")
500		if err := c.Start(); err != nil {
501			firstErr = errnoName(errors.Unwrap(err))
502			if firstErr == "error" {
503				firstErr = err.Error()
504			}
505			break
506		}
507		kids = append(kids, c)
508		started++
509	}
510	for _, c := range kids {
511		_ = c.Wait()
512	}
513	out := map[string]any{"requested": n, "started": started, "first_error": firstErr}
514	_ = json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout).Encode(out)
515	return 0
516}

518func memtest(mib int) int {
519	chunks := make([][]byte, 0, mib)
520	for i := 1; i <= mib; i++ {
521		b := make([]byte, 1<<20)
522		for j := 0; j < len(b); j += 4096 {
523			b[j] = 1
524		}
525		chunks = append(chunks, b)
526		if i%16 == 0 || i == mib {
527			fmt.Printf("{\"touched_mib\":%d}\n", i)
528		}
529	}
530	runtime.KeepAlive(chunks)
531	return 0
532}

534// ---- Kubernetes workload-identity probe ---------------------------------------
535 
536// K8sCall is one API request outcome. Only the HTTP status and, for a list, the
537// number of items are recorded: never object names or contents, so running the
538// probe against an over-privileged identity does not print secret material.
539type K8sCall struct {
540	Name   string `json:"name"`
541	Status int    `json:"status"`
542	Items  *int   `json:"items,omitempty"`
543	Error  string `json:"error,omitempty"`
544}
545 
546// K8sReport is the full `k8sprobe` output.
547type K8sReport struct {
548	TokenMounted bool                   `json:"token_mounted"`
549	Namespace    string                 `json:"namespace,omitempty"`
550	Claims       map[string]interface{} `json:"token_claims,omitempty"`
551	Calls        []K8sCall              `json:"api_calls,omitempty"`
552	Access       map[string]bool        `json:"self_subject_access_review,omitempty"`
553	Note         string                 `json:"note,omitempty"`
554}
555 
556// jwtClaims decodes the payload of a service-account JWT WITHOUT verifying it.
557// It is informational (what the pod was handed); the API server is the verifier.
558func jwtClaims(token string) map[string]interface{} {
559	parts := strings.Split(token, ".")
560	if len(parts) != 3 {
561		return nil
562	}
563	raw, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(parts[1])
564	if err != nil {
565		return nil
566	}
567	var all map[string]interface{}
568	if json.Unmarshal(raw, &all) != nil {
569		return nil
570	}
571	out := map[string]interface{}{"sub": all["sub"], "aud": all["aud"], "iss": all["iss"]}
572	if exp, ok := all["exp"].(float64); ok {
573		out["seconds_until_expiry"] = int64(exp) - time.Now().Unix()
574	}
575	if iat, ok := all["iat"].(float64); ok {
576		out["token_age_seconds"] = time.Now().Unix() - int64(iat)
577	}
578	// A bound token carries the pod it was issued to; a legacy secret-based token does not.
579	if kube, ok := all["kubernetes.io"].(map[string]interface{}); ok {
580		_, bound := kube["pod"]
581		out["bound_to_pod"] = bound
582	} else {
583		out["bound_to_pod"] = false
584	}
585	return out
586}
587 
588func k8sprobe() int {
589	const dir = "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount"
590	rep := K8sReport{}
591	emit := func() int {
592		enc := json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout)
593		enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
594		_ = enc.Encode(rep)
595		return 0
596	}
597	tokenBytes, err := os.ReadFile(dir + "/token")
598	if err != nil {
599		rep.Note = "no service-account token mounted at " + dir
600		return emit()
601	}
602	rep.TokenMounted = true
603	token := strings.TrimSpace(string(tokenBytes))
604	rep.Namespace = readTrim(dir + "/namespace")
605	rep.Claims = jwtClaims(token)
606 
607	caPEM, err := os.ReadFile(dir + "/ca.crt")
608	pool := x509.NewCertPool()
609	if err != nil || !pool.AppendCertsFromPEM(caPEM) {
610		rep.Note = "cannot load cluster CA"
611		return emit()
612	}
613	host, port := os.Getenv("KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST"), os.Getenv("KUBERNETES_SERVICE_PORT")
614	if host == "" || port == "" {
615		rep.Note = "KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST/PORT not set"
616		return emit()
617	}
618	base := "https://" + net.JoinHostPort(host, port)
619	client := &http.Client{
620		Timeout:   3 * time.Second,
621		Transport: &http.Transport{TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{RootCAs: pool, MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS12}},
622	}
623	do := func(method, path string, body []byte) (int, []byte, error) {
624		req, _ := http.NewRequest(method, base+path, bytes.NewReader(body))
625		req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
626		if body != nil {
627			req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
628		}
629		resp, err := client.Do(req)
630		if err != nil {
631			return 0, nil, err
632		}
633		defer resp.Body.Close()
634		data, _ := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 4<<20))
635		return resp.StatusCode, data, nil
636	}
637 
638	ns := rep.Namespace
639	reads := []struct{ name, path string }{
640		{"get_configmap_app_config_own_ns", "/api/v1/namespaces/" + ns + "/configmaps/app-config"},
641		{"list_configmaps_own_ns", "/api/v1/namespaces/" + ns + "/configmaps"},
642		{"list_secrets_own_ns", "/api/v1/namespaces/" + ns + "/secrets"},
643		{"list_secrets_kube_system", "/api/v1/namespaces/kube-system/secrets"},
644		{"list_pods_all_namespaces", "/api/v1/pods"},
645		{"list_nodes", "/api/v1/nodes"},
646	}
647	for _, r := range reads {
648		status, data, err := do(http.MethodGet, r.path, nil)
649		call := K8sCall{Name: r.name, Status: status}
650		if err != nil {
651			call.Error = errnoName(errors.Unwrap(err))
652			if call.Error == "error" {
653				call.Error = "request failed (network or TLS)"
654			}
655		} else if status == http.StatusOK {
656			var list struct {
657				Items []json.RawMessage `json:"items"`
658			}
659			if json.Unmarshal(data, &list) == nil && list.Items != nil {
660				n := len(list.Items)
661				call.Items = &n
662			}
663		}
664		rep.Calls = append(rep.Calls, call)
665	}
666 
667	// Write permissions are checked with SelfSubjectAccessReview: asks the API
668	// server whether the action WOULD be allowed, and creates nothing.
669	rep.Access = map[string]bool{}
670	reviews := []struct{ name, verb, group, resource, sub, namespace string }{
671		{"create_pods_own_ns", "create", "", "pods", "", ns},
672		{"create_pods_exec_own_ns", "create", "", "pods", "exec", ns},
673		{"get_secrets_any_namespace", "get", "", "secrets", "", ""},
674		{"create_rolebindings_own_ns", "create", "rbac.authorization.k8s.io", "rolebindings", "", ns},
675		{"escalate_clusterroles", "escalate", "rbac.authorization.k8s.io", "clusterroles", "", ""},
676		{"impersonate_users", "impersonate", "", "users", "", ""},
677	}
678	for _, rv := range reviews {
679		attrs := map[string]string{"verb": rv.verb, "group": rv.group, "resource": rv.resource}
680		if rv.sub != "" {
681			attrs["subresource"] = rv.sub
682		}
683		if rv.namespace != "" {
684			attrs["namespace"] = rv.namespace
685		}
686		body, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]interface{}{
687			"apiVersion": "authorization.k8s.io/v1", "kind": "SelfSubjectAccessReview",
688			"spec": map[string]interface{}{"resourceAttributes": attrs},
689		})
690		status, data, err := do(http.MethodPost, "/apis/authorization.k8s.io/v1/selfsubjectaccessreviews", body)
691		allowed := false
692		if err == nil && status == http.StatusCreated {
693			var out struct {
694				Status struct {
695					Allowed bool `json:"allowed"`
696				} `json:"status"`
697			}
698			if json.Unmarshal(data, &out) == nil {
699				allowed = out.Status.Allowed
700			}
701		}
702		rep.Access[rv.name] = allowed
703	}
704	return emit()
705}
706 
707// tcpcheck makes one TCP connection attempt and reports it. The distroless image
708// has no shell, nc or curl, so reachability tests need to live in the binary.
709func tcpcheck(target string) int {
710	out := map[string]interface{}{"target": target, "connected": false}
711	conn, err := net.DialTimeout("tcp", target, 3*time.Second)
712	if err == nil {
713		conn.Close()
714		out["connected"] = true
715	} else {
716		var dnsErr *net.DNSError
717		var netErr net.Error
718		switch {
719		case errors.As(err, &dnsErr):
720			out["error"] = "name resolution failed"
721		case errors.As(err, &netErr) && netErr.Timeout():
722			out["error"] = "timeout"
723		default:
724			out["error"] = errnoName(errors.Unwrap(errors.Unwrap(err)))
725		}
726	}
727	_ = json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout).Encode(out)
728	return 0
729}
    1#!/usr/bin/env node
2"use strict";
3 
4/**
5 * Static policy gate for Dockerfiles and Compose files (no Docker required).
6 *
7 * This is deliberately a small, readable rule set that encodes the control
8 * decisions in the lab README. It is NOT a replacement for a maintained
9 * misconfiguration scanner; the lab runs Trivy as well and records where the
10 * two disagree. Every rule has a positive and a negative test in
11 * policy-check.test.js.
12 *
13 * Usage: node policy-check.js <dir-or-file>...   (exit 1 when any finding exists)
14 */
15 
16const fs = require("node:fs");
17const path = require("node:path");
18const YAML = require("yaml");
19 
20const DANGEROUS_CAPS = new Set([
21  "ALL", "SYS_ADMIN", "NET_ADMIN", "SYS_PTRACE", "SYS_MODULE", "SYS_RAWIO",
22  "DAC_READ_SEARCH", "SYS_BOOT", "MAC_ADMIN", "BPF", "PERFMON",
23]);
24const SENSITIVE_HOST_PATHS = ["/", "/etc", "/proc", "/sys", "/dev", "/root", "/home", "/var/lib/docker", "/var/run", "/run"];
25const SECRET_NAME = /(PASSWORD|PASSWD|SECRET|TOKEN|API_?KEY|PRIVATE_?KEY|ACCESS_?KEY)/i;
26 
27/** Logical Dockerfile instructions (line continuations joined, comments dropped). */
28function parseDockerfile(source) {
29  const lines = source.split(/\r?\n/);
30  const out = [];
31  let buffer = "";
32  let startLine = 0;
33  lines.forEach((raw, index) => {
34    const trimmed = raw.trim();
35    if (!buffer && (trimmed === "" || trimmed.startsWith("#"))) return;
36    if (!buffer) startLine = index + 1;
37    const continued = trimmed.endsWith("\\");
38    buffer += (buffer ? " " : "") + (continued ? trimmed.slice(0, -1).trim() : trimmed);
39    if (!continued) {
40      const space = buffer.search(/\s/);
41      const instruction = (space === -1 ? buffer : buffer.slice(0, space)).toUpperCase();
42      const args = space === -1 ? "" : buffer.slice(space + 1).trim();
43      out.push({ instruction, args, line: startLine });
44      buffer = "";
45    }
46  });
47  return out;
48}
49 
50function analyzeDockerfile(source, file = "Dockerfile") {
51  const findings = [];
52  const add = (rule, line, message) => findings.push({ file, rule, line, message });
53  const items = parseDockerfile(source);
54  const froms = items.filter((item) => item.instruction === "FROM");
55 
56  for (const from of froms) {
57    const ref = from.args.replace(/^--platform=\S+\s+/, "").split(/\s+/)[0];
58    const stageRefs = froms.map((candidate) => (candidate.args.match(/\bAS\s+(\S+)/i) || [])[1]).filter(Boolean);
59    if (stageRefs.includes(ref) || ref === "scratch") continue;
60    if (!ref.includes("@sha256:")) add("DF001", from.line, `base image ${ref} is not pinned by digest`);
61    const tag = ref.split("@")[0].split("/").pop();
62    if (!tag.includes(":") || tag.endsWith(":latest")) add("DF002", from.line, `base image ${ref} uses latest or an implicit tag`);
63  }
64 
65  if (froms.length) {
66    const finalStart = items.indexOf(froms[froms.length - 1]);
67    const finalStage = items.slice(finalStart);
68    const users = finalStage.filter((item) => item.instruction === "USER");
69    const lastUser = users.length ? users[users.length - 1].args.split(/\s+/)[0].split(":")[0] : null;
70    if (!lastUser || lastUser === "root" || lastUser === "0") add("DF003", froms[froms.length - 1].line, "final stage runs as root (no non-root USER)");
71    if (!finalStage.some((item) => item.instruction === "HEALTHCHECK")) add("DF006", froms[froms.length - 1].line, "final stage defines no HEALTHCHECK");
72    for (const item of finalStage) {
73      if ((item.instruction === "CMD" || item.instruction === "ENTRYPOINT") && !item.args.startsWith("[")) {
74        add("DF007", item.line, `${item.instruction} uses shell form; PID 1 will be a shell that does not forward signals`);
75      }
76    }
77    if (froms.length === 1 && items.some((item) => item.instruction === "RUN" && /\b(go build|npm (ci|install)|pip3? install|apt-get install|apk add|make|gcc)\b/.test(item.args))) {
78      add("DF009", froms[0].line, "single-stage build: compiler or package manager ships in the runtime image");
79    }
80  }
81 
82  for (const item of items) {
83    if ((item.instruction === "ENV" || item.instruction === "ARG")) {
84      const match = item.args.match(/^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)(?:=|\s+)(.+)$/);
85      if (match && SECRET_NAME.test(match[1]) && match[2].replace(/["']/g, "").trim() !== "") {
86        add("DF004", item.line, `${item.instruction} ${match[1]} carries a literal value; it persists in image metadata`);
87      }
88    }
89    if (item.instruction === "RUN" && /\bchmod\b[^;&|]*\b(-R\s+)?(0?777|a\+rwx)\b/.test(item.args)) add("DF005", item.line, "world-writable permissions set in the image");
90    if (item.instruction === "ADD" && /^(--\S+\s+)*https?:\/\//.test(item.args)) add("DF008", item.line, "ADD from a remote URL is neither pinned nor verified");
91    if (item.instruction === "RUN" && /(curl|wget)[^|;&]*\|\s*(sudo\s+)?(sh|bash)\b/.test(item.args)) add("DF008", item.line, "pipes a downloaded script into a shell");
92  }
93  return findings;
94}
95 
96function asList(value) {
97  if (value === undefined || value === null) return [];
98  return Array.isArray(value) ? value : Object.entries(value).map(([k, v]) => `${k}=${v}`);
99}
100 
101/** Split "source:target[:mode]" where source may be a ${VAR:?message} expression. */
102function splitVolume(spec) {
103  const match = spec.match(/^(\$\{[^}]*\}|[^:]+):(.*)$/);
104  return match ? { source: match[1], rest: match[2] } : { source: spec, rest: "" };
105}
106 
107function normalizeCap(cap) {
108  return String(cap).toUpperCase().replace(/^CAP_/, "");
109}
110 
111function analyzeCompose(source, file = "compose.yaml") {
112  const findings = [];
113  const document = YAML.parse(source) || {};
114  const services = document.services || {};
115  for (const [name, service] of Object.entries(services)) {
116    const add = (rule, message) => findings.push({ file, service: name, rule, message });
117    const local = service.build !== undefined;
118    const image = service.image || "";
119 
120    if (service.privileged === true) add("DC001", "privileged: true grants all capabilities and device access");
121    const capAdd = asList(service.cap_add).map(normalizeCap);
122    for (const cap of capAdd) if (DANGEROUS_CAPS.has(cap)) add("DC002", `cap_add ${cap}`);
123    const capDrop = asList(service.cap_drop).map(normalizeCap);
124    if (!capDrop.includes("ALL")) add("DC003", "cap_drop does not include ALL");
125 
126    const securityOpt = asList(service.security_opt).map(String);
127    if (securityOpt.some((opt) => /^(seccomp|apparmor)[=:]unconfined$/.test(opt))) add("DC004", "seccomp or AppArmor confinement disabled");
128    if (!securityOpt.some((opt) => /^no-new-privileges(:|=)true$/.test(opt) || opt === "no-new-privileges")) add("DC005", "no-new-privileges is not set");
129 
130    for (const volume of asList(service.volumes)) {
131      const spec = typeof volume === "string" ? volume : `${volume.source}:${volume.target}${volume.read_only ? ":ro" : ""}`;
132      const { source, rest } = splitVolume(spec);
133      if (/(docker|podman|containerd|crio)\.sock(:|$)/.test(spec)) add("DC006", "container runtime socket mounted (host-root equivalent; :ro on a socket file does not restrict API calls)");
134      else if (source.startsWith("/") || source.startsWith("${") || source.startsWith(".")) {
135        const normalized = path.posix.normalize(source);
136        if (SENSITIVE_HOST_PATHS.includes(normalized)) add("DC007", `sensitive host path ${normalized} bind-mounted`);
137        else if (!/(^|:)ro(,|$)/.test(rest.split(":").slice(1).join(":"))) add("DC007", `host bind mount ${source} is writable`);
138      }
139    }
140 
141    for (const key of ["pid", "ipc", "uts", "userns_mode", "network_mode"]) {
142      if (service[key] === "host") add("DC008", `${key}: host shares a host namespace`);
143    }
144 
145    const user = service.user === undefined ? "" : String(service.user);
146    if (!user || user === "root" || user.split(":")[0] === "0") add("DC009", "container user is root or unset");
147    if (service.read_only !== true) add("DC010", "root filesystem is writable (read_only is not true)");
148    const limits = (service.deploy && service.deploy.resources && service.deploy.resources.limits) || {};
149    if (!service.mem_limit && !limits.memory) add("DC011", "no memory limit");
150    if (!service.pids_limit && !limits.pids) add("DC012", "no PID limit");
151    if (!service.cpus && !limits.cpus && !service.cpu_quota) add("DC013", "no CPU limit");
152 
153    for (const port of asList(service.ports)) {
154      const spec = typeof port === "string" ? port : `${port.host_ip || ""}:${port.published}:${port.target}`;
155      const parts = spec.split(":");
156      const hostIp = parts.length >= 3 ? parts[0] : "";
157      if (hostIp !== "127.0.0.1" && hostIp !== "::1") add("DC014", `published port ${spec} binds all interfaces`);
158    }
159 
160    if (!local && image && !image.includes("@sha256:")) add("DC015", `external image ${image} is not pinned by digest`);
161    if (!local && /:latest$/.test(image)) add("DC016", `external image ${image} uses latest`);
162  }
163  return findings;
164}
165 
166function collect(target) {
167  const stat = fs.statSync(target);
168  if (stat.isDirectory()) {
169    return fs.readdirSync(target).sort().flatMap((entry) => collect(path.join(target, entry)));
170  }
171  return [target];
172}
173 
174function analyzePath(target) {
175  const findings = [];
176  for (const file of collect(target)) {
177    const base = path.basename(file);
178    const text = () => fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8");
179    if (base === "Dockerfile" || base.startsWith("Dockerfile.")) findings.push(...analyzeDockerfile(text(), file));
180    else if (/^(docker-)?compose(\.[\w-]+)?\.ya?ml$/.test(base)) findings.push(...analyzeCompose(text(), file));
181  }
182  return findings;
183}
184 
185module.exports = { analyzeCompose, analyzeDockerfile, analyzePath, parseDockerfile };
186 
187if (require.main === module) {
188  const targets = process.argv.slice(2);
189  if (!targets.length) {
190    console.error("usage: policy-check.js <dir-or-file>...");
191    process.exit(2);
192  }
193  const findings = targets.flatMap(analyzePath);
194  for (const f of findings) {
195    const where = f.line ? `${f.file}:${f.line}` : `${f.file} [${f.service}]`;
196    console.log(`${f.rule}  ${where}  ${f.message}`);
197  }
198  console.log(`${findings.length} finding(s)`);
199  process.exit(findings.length ? 1 : 0);
200}

23    ports: ["127.0.0.1:8080:8080"]

26function composeWith(extra) {
27  return GOOD_SERVICE.replace("    build: .\n", `    build: .\n${extra}`);

34// ---- Compose rules: each is triggered by exactly its own mutation ----------
35const composeCases = [
36  ["DC001", "    privileged: true\n"],

50for (const [rule, mutation] of composeCases) {

52    // Mutations that replace an existing key are applied by overriding via text edit.

57  });

84const PINNED = `sha256:${"b".repeat(64)}`;
85const GOOD_DOCKERFILE = `

90USER 65532:65532
91HEALTHCHECK CMD ["/app/app", "healthcheck"]
92ENTRYPOINT ["/app/app"]

137  const found = ids(analyzePath(path.join(lab, "insecure")));
138  for (const required of [
139    "DF001", "DF003", "DF004", "DF005", "DF006", "DF007", "DF009",

151test("the hardened stack's seccomp profile is default-deny and does not allow escape-relevant syscalls", () => {
152  const profile = require(path.join(lab, "hardened", "seccomp.json"));
153  assert.equal(profile.defaultAction, "SCMP_ACT_ERRNO");
154  const allowed = new Set(
155    profile.syscalls.filter((rule) => rule.action === "SCMP_ACT_ALLOW").flatMap((rule) => rule.names),
156  );
157  for (const name of [
158    "mount", "umount2", "setns", "unshare", "ptrace", "bpf", "keyctl", "perf_event_open",
159    "userfaultfd", "kexec_load", "init_module", "finit_module", "open_by_handle_at",
160    "pivot_root", "chroot", "reboot", "mknodat", "fchownat", "fsopen", "fsmount", "move_mount",
161  ]) {
162    assert.ok(!allowed.has(name), `${name} must not be allowlisted`);
163  }
164  // clone is allowed only with a namespace-flag mask; clone3 must fall back via ENOSYS.
165  const cloneRule = profile.syscalls.find((rule) => rule.names.includes("clone"));
166  assert.equal(cloneRule.args[0].op, "SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ");
167  assert.equal(cloneRule.args[0].value, 0x7e020000);
168  assert.equal(cloneRule.args[0].valueTwo, 0);
169  const clone3Rule = profile.syscalls.find((rule) => rule.names.includes("clone3"));
170  assert.equal(clone3Rule.action, "SCMP_ACT_ERRNO");
171  assert.equal(clone3Rule.errnoRet, 38);
172  // The service must still be able to serve: sockets and the runtime hand-off set.
173  for (const name of ["socket", "bind", "listen", "accept4", "fstatfs", "statx", "execve"]) {
174    assert.ok(allowed.has(name), `${name} must be allowlisted for the service to start`);
175  }
176});
    1#!/usr/bin/env python3
2"""Assert the OBSERVED runtime results of the Docker lab. Usage: runtime_check.py <outdir>
3 
4Reads the JSON that scripts/run-lab.sh wrote and fails (exit 1) when any claimed
5control is not what the running container actually reported. Supply-chain
6assertions run only when those steps executed; otherwise they print SKIP with the
7recorded reason - a skip is never reported as a pass.
8"""
9import json
10import pathlib
11import sys
12 
13out = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
14failures = []
15passes = 0
16 
17 
18def load(rel):
19    path = out / rel
20    return json.loads(path.read_text()) if path.exists() else None
21 
22 
23def check(name, condition, detail=""):
24    global passes
25    if condition:
26        passes += 1
27        print(f"PASS  {name}")
28    else:
29        failures.append(name)
30        print(f"FAIL  {name}  {detail}")
31 
32 
33def probes(report):
34    return {p["name"].split(" ")[0]: p for p in report["probes"]}
35 
36 
37def read_exit(rel):
38    path = out / rel
39    return int(path.read_text().strip()) if path.exists() else None
40 
41 
42# ---- insecure baseline: every dangerous capability is observable --------------
43ins = load("runtime/insecure-probe.json")
44check("insecure: probe output exists", ins is not None)
45if ins:
46    p, pr = ins["posture"], probes(ins)
47    check("insecure: runs as uid 0", p["uid"] == 0, p["uid"])
48    check("insecure: large effective capability set (privileged)", len(p["cap_eff"]) >= 30, len(p["cap_eff"]))
49    check("insecure: SYS_ADMIN present", "SYS_ADMIN" in p["cap_eff"])
50    check("insecure: no_new_privs off", p["no_new_privs"] == "0", p["no_new_privs"])
51    check("insecure: seccomp off", p["seccomp_mode"] == "0", p["seccomp_mode"])
52    check("insecure: root filesystem writable", p["root_fs_mounted_read_only"] is False)
53    check("insecure: no memory limit", "9223372036854771712" in p["memory_limit"] or p["memory_limit"].startswith("max"), p["memory_limit"])
54    check("insecure: no pids limit", p["pids_limit"].startswith("max"), p["pids_limit"])
55    check("insecure: host PID namespace visible", p["pid1_comm"] != "posture" and p["visible_process_count"] > 10, (p["pid1_comm"], p["visible_process_count"]))
56    for name in ("write_root_filesystem", "write_tmp_scratch", "chown_to_other_uid", "mknod_char_device",
57                 "raw_socket", "mount_tmpfs", "clone_new_user_namespace", "docker_socket_reachable",
58                 "host_canary_read", "host_canary_write", "tcp_connect_canary"):
59        check(f"insecure: {name} allowed", pr.get(name, {}).get("allowed") is True, pr.get(name))
60    check("insecure: docker API answered /_ping", "200 OK" in pr.get("docker_socket_reachable", {}).get("detail", ""))
61    fork = load("runtime/insecure-forktest.json")
62    check("insecure: all 200 children started (no PID limit)", bool(fork) and fork["started"] == fork["requested"], fork)
63    check("insecure: 512 MiB allocation succeeds (no memory limit)", read_exit("runtime/insecure-memtest.exit") == 0)
64    owner = (out / "runtime/insecure-host-canary-owner.txt")
65    check("insecure: file written into the bind-mounted host directory is owned by uid 0",
66          owner.exists() and owner.read_text().split()[0] == "0", owner.read_text() if owner.exists() else None)
67 
68# ---- hardened: the same probes are refused -------------------------------------
69har = load("runtime/hardened-probe.json")
70check("hardened: probe output exists", har is not None)
71if har:
72    p, pr = har["posture"], probes(har)
73    check("hardened: runs as uid 65532", p["uid"] == 65532, p["uid"])
74    check("hardened: effective capability set is empty", p["cap_eff"] == [], p["cap_eff"])
75    check("hardened: no_new_privs on", p["no_new_privs"] == "1", p["no_new_privs"])
76    check("hardened: seccomp filter active", p["seccomp_mode"] == "2" and p["seccomp_filters"] == "1", (p["seccomp_mode"], p["seccomp_filters"]))
77    check("hardened: root filesystem read-only", p["root_fs_mounted_read_only"] is True)
78    check("hardened: memory limit 128 MiB", p["memory_limit"].startswith("134217728"), p["memory_limit"])
79    check("hardened: pids limit 64", p["pids_limit"].startswith("64"), p["pids_limit"])
80    check("hardened: cpu quota 0.5 CPU", p["cpu_quota"].startswith("50000"), p["cpu_quota"])
81    check("hardened: own PID namespace (app is PID 1, few processes)", p["pid1_comm"] == "posture" and p["visible_process_count"] < 10, (p["pid1_comm"], p["visible_process_count"]))
82    expect_denied = {
83        "write_root_filesystem": "EROFS", "chown_to_other_uid": "EPERM", "mknod_char_device": "EPERM",
84        "raw_socket": "EPERM", "mount_tmpfs": "EPERM", "clone_new_user_namespace": "EPERM",
85        "docker_socket_present": "ENOENT", "host_canary_mounted": "ENOENT",
86    }
87    for name, errno in expect_denied.items():
88        got = pr.get(name, {})
89        check(f"hardened: {name} denied with {errno}", got.get("allowed") is False and got.get("errno") == errno, got)
90    check("hardened: scratch tmpfs still writable (the app is not broken)", pr["write_tmp_scratch"]["allowed"] is True)
91    canary = pr.get("tcp_connect_canary", {})
92    check("hardened: canary unreachable and name not resolvable (network topology)", canary.get("allowed") is False and "name resolution failed" in canary.get("detail", ""), canary)
93    health = out / "runtime/hardened-health-before.txt"
94    check("hardened: container reported healthy via image HEALTHCHECK", health.exists() and health.read_text().strip() == "healthy")
95    fork = load("runtime/hardened-forktest.json")
96    check("hardened: PID limit stops child creation with EAGAIN", bool(fork) and fork["started"] < fork["requested"] and fork["first_error"] == "EAGAIN", fork)
97    mem = read_exit("runtime/hardened-memtest.exit")
98    check("hardened: 512 MiB allocation is OOM-killed under a 128 MiB limit (exit 137)", mem == 137, mem)
99 
100# ---- seccomp attribution controls (same hardening, different seccomp setting) ---
101for label, mode, clone_allowed in (("unconfined", "0", True), ("default", "2", False), ("custom", "2", False)):
102    ctl = load(f"runtime/hardened-seccomp-{label}-probe.json")
103    check(f"control seccomp={label}: probe output exists", ctl is not None)
104    if ctl:
105        clone = probes(ctl)["clone_new_user_namespace"]
106        check(f"control seccomp={label}: seccomp_mode {mode}", ctl["posture"]["seccomp_mode"] == mode, ctl["posture"]["seccomp_mode"])
107        check(f"control seccomp={label}: user-namespace clone {'allowed' if clone_allowed else 'denied'}",
108              clone["allowed"] is clone_allowed, clone)
109        check(f"control seccomp={label}: capabilities still empty (so the denial is not a capability effect)", ctl["posture"]["cap_eff"] == [])
110 
111# ---- attack surface of the image filesystems ---------------------------------------
112inv_i, inv_h = load("runtime/insecure-inventory.json"), load("runtime/hardened-inventory.json")
113check("inventory: both images inventoried", inv_i is not None and inv_h is not None)
114if inv_i and inv_h:
115    check("inventory: insecure image ships a shell", bool(inv_i["shells"]), inv_i["shells"])
116    check("inventory: insecure image ships a package manager", bool(inv_i["package_managers"]), inv_i["package_managers"])
117    check("inventory: insecure image ships a compiler/toolchain", "usr/local/go/bin/go" in inv_i["compilers_or_interpreters"], inv_i["compilers_or_interpreters"])
118    check("inventory: hardened image ships no shell", inv_h["shells"] == [], inv_h["shells"])
119    check("inventory: hardened image ships no package manager", inv_h["package_managers"] == [], inv_h["package_managers"])
120    check("inventory: hardened image ships no compiler or interpreter", inv_h["compilers_or_interpreters"] == [], inv_h["compilers_or_interpreters"])
121    check("inventory: hardened image has no setuid/setgid files", inv_h["setuid_or_setgid"] == [], inv_h["setuid_or_setgid"])
122    check("inventory: hardened image has far fewer executable files", inv_h["executables"] * 5 < inv_i["executables"], (inv_h["executables"], inv_i["executables"]))
123    print(f"INFO  inventory: executables insecure={inv_i['executables']} hardened={inv_h['executables']}; "
124          f"size insecure={inv_i['size_bytes']} hardened={inv_h['size_bytes']} bytes (file content)")
125 
126# ---- supply chain (only when executed) -----------------------------------------
127scan = load("scan/summary.json")
128if scan and scan.get("trivy", {}).get("version"):
129    imgs = scan["images"]
130    ins_n = imgs["insecure"]["unique_cve_package_pairs"]
131    har_n = imgs["hardened"]["unique_cve_package_pairs"]
132    # Deliberately NOT asserting hardened < insecure: CVE counts do not rank
133    # attack surface (the observed result is the opposite - see README).
134    print(f"INFO  scan: unique CVE/package findings insecure={ins_n} hardened={har_n} "
135          "(a count of known CVEs is not an attack-surface measure)")
136    for variant in ("insecure", "hardened"):
137        entry = imgs[variant]
138        check(f"scan: {variant} summary is internally consistent",
139              entry["raw_findings"] >= entry["unique_cve_package_pairs"] and sum(entry["unique_by_severity"].values()) == entry["unique_cve_package_pairs"], entry)
140    check("scan: SBOM-only scan agrees with the image scan for both variants",
141          all(scan["sbom"][v]["unique_findings_from_sbom_only"] == imgs[v]["unique_cve_package_pairs"] for v in ("insecure", "hardened") if v in scan["sbom"]),
142          {v: (scan["sbom"][v]["unique_findings_from_sbom_only"], imgs[v]["unique_cve_package_pairs"]) for v in scan["sbom"]})
143    mis_i = scan["dockerfile_misconfigurations"].get("insecure", [])
144    mis_h = scan["dockerfile_misconfigurations"].get("hardened", [])
145    check("scan: Trivy flags the insecure Dockerfile (root user, no HEALTHCHECK, secret in ENV)",
146          {"DS-0002", "DS-0026", "DS-0031"} <= {m["id"] for m in mis_i}, mis_i)
147    check("scan: Trivy reports nothing for the hardened Dockerfile", mis_h == [], mis_h)
148    check("scan: Trivy DB timestamp recorded", bool(scan["trivy"].get("db_updated_at")), scan["trivy"])
149else:
150    print("SKIP  scan: Trivy was not executed (see scan/status.json)")
151if scan and scan.get("sbom"):
152    for variant, sbom in scan["sbom"].items():
153        check(f"sbom: {variant} CycloneDX document has components", sbom["components"] > 0 and sbom["format"] == "CycloneDX", sbom)
154else:
155    print("SKIP  sbom: Syft was not executed (see sbom/status.json)")
156 
157sign = load("signing/summary.json")
158if sign and sign.get("executed"):
159    for key, want in (("signed", True), ("verify_signed_digest", True), ("unsigned_rejected", True),
160                      ("wrong_key_rejected", True), ("tag_before_substitution_ok", True),
161                      ("tag_substitution_rejected", True), ("attestation_verified", True),
162                      ("wrong_predicate_rejected", True)):
163        if key in sign["results"]:
164            check(f"signing: {key}", sign["results"][key] is want, sign["results"][key])
165else:
166    print("SKIP  signing: cosign was not executed (see signing/status.json)")
167 
168print(f"\n{passes} passed, {len(failures)} failed")
169sys.exit(1 if failures else 0)

    Run it

    • node --test labs/docker-security/tests/policy-check.test.js
    • bash labs/docker-security/scripts/run-lab.sh

    Status: partially tested. The static policy gate runs anywhere and is part of npm run validate. The runtime, scanning, SBOM and signing steps ran on one disposable VM on 2026-11-05 (85 of 85 assertions passed) and are not wired into CI. AppArmor, rootless Docker, user-namespace remapping and a production signing trust root were not executed (see What was not tested).

    Evidence labels used on this page:

    Label Meaning Closest tier in the evidence standards
    tested locally I ran it in this lab and kept the output in evidence/ T2/T3, T4 where the same case ran on both stacks
    source-reviewed I read it in the named primary source; not executed here T0
    policy model A rule set evaluated by a local test, not enforced by the real system T1
    requires-review No independent reviewer has checked it against its sources review status of this page

    Scope¶

    One service, two configurations, one question: what can code running inside the container do, and what changes when the controls are on? The service is a Go program of about 730 lines (standard library only) (app/main.go) with an HTTP endpoint and a probe subcommand that tries a fixed list of benign operations (write the root filesystem, chown, mknod, open a raw socket, mount, create a user namespace, reach the Docker socket, write a bind-mounted directory, open a TCP connection) and reports the errno the kernel returned. Observing denials from inside the container is the point; reading a Compose file and assuming it took effect is how hardening claims go wrong.

    In scope: image build, base-image choice, user, filesystem, capabilities, no-new-privileges, seccomp, resource limits, network topology, image scanning, SBOM, signing and verification by digest.

    Out of scope: Kubernetes (see the Kubernetes lab), runtime detection tooling, registry operations, host hardening and anything that targets systems I do not own. Nothing here contacts a real cloud account, production system or third-party service other than downloading base images and the Trivy vulnerability database.

    Safety. The insecure stack runs privileged: true, pid: host and mounts the Docker socket on purpose. Run run-lab.sh only on a throwaway VM or CI runner. The probe sends one read-only GET /_ping to the socket and nothing else; it creates no containers and changes no host state outside a temp directory the script owns.

    What I built¶

    Path Purpose
    app/ Go (stdlib only) service with probe, healthcheck, forktest, memtest subcommands, plus k8sprobe and tcpcheck, which the Kubernetes lab reuses
    insecure/Dockerfile, insecure/compose.yaml Deliberately bad baseline; every line maps to a rule the gate must report
    hardened/Dockerfile, hardened/compose.yaml Same service, controls on
    hardened/seccomp.json Allowlist profile derived from strace of the shipped binary
    scripts/gen-seccomp.sh Derives the profile; prints which syscalls were service, harness, hand-off or removed
    scripts/run-lab.sh Builds, runs both stacks, runs controls, scans, signs, asserts, optionally publishes evidence
    scripts/scan.sh, scripts/sign-verify.sh Trivy + Syft; local registry + cosign with an ephemeral key
    tests/policy-check.js (+ .test.js) Static Dockerfile/Compose gate; 38 tests, a positive and a negative case per rule
    tests/runtime_check.py, inventory.py, summarize_scan.py Assertions on observed output, image attack-surface inventory, scan dedup
    evidence/ Sanitized output of the run described below 
    flowchart LR
  subgraph BUILD["Build"]
    SRC["app source"] --> B1["builder stage<br/>digest-pinned Go image"]
    B1 --> IMG["static binary on<br/>distroless nonroot"]
  end
  subgraph ASSURE["Scan and sign"]
    IMG --> SG["static policy gate<br/>Dockerfile and Compose"]
    IMG --> TR["Trivy image scan<br/>Dockerfile misconfig"]
    IMG --> SY["Syft SBOM<br/>CycloneDX"]
    SY --> TS["Trivy SBOM-only scan"]
    IMG --> CS["cosign sign by digest"]
    SY --> CA["cosign attest SBOM"]
  end
  subgraph DEPLOY["Deploy"]
    CS --> VF{"verify digest<br/>before run"}
    CA --> VF
    VF -->|"signature missing or key wrong"| STOP["reject"]
    VF -->|"ok"| RUN["compose up"]
  end
  subgraph RUNTIME["Runtime enforcement"]
    RUN --> U["non-root uid 65532"]
    RUN --> C["cap_drop ALL"]
    RUN --> N["no-new-privileges"]
    RUN --> S["seccomp allowlist"]
    RUN --> R["read-only rootfs + tmpfs"]
    RUN --> L["memory, PIDs, CPU limits"]
    RUN --> NET["internal network"]
  end

    Status: the pipeline in this diagram is a design diagram. Every box except "verify digest before run" was executed by run-lab.sh; verification was executed as a command (cosign verify) but nothing in this lab refuses to start an unsigned image. Enforcement at deploy time needs an admission controller or a deploy wrapper; the Kubernetes lab models that decision.

    Attack surface and threat model¶

    Element Declared scope
    Actor Code running as the container's main process: a compromised dependency, an RCE in the service, or a malicious image layer
    Assets The host kernel and filesystem, the Docker daemon, neighbouring containers, the service's own data
    Entry points Anything the process can call: syscalls, mounted paths, sockets, network
    Trust boundary Container process → kernel (namespaces, capabilities, seccomp, cgroups) → host
    Not in scope A kernel vulnerability or runc escape; hardening reduces reachable kernel surface but cannot make a shared kernel a hard multi-tenant boundary

    The insecure configuration is built to expose each of these at once: root, full capability set, no syscall filter, host PID namespace, Docker socket, writable bind mount, writable root filesystem, no limits, all-interface port.

    Control decisions¶

    Each row names what the control prevents and what it does not. The last column is the cost I would expect to pay.

    Control Insecure Hardened Stops Does not stop Cost / false-positive risk
    Base image golang:1.27-alpine (toolchain, apk, shell ship in runtime), tag only distroless static-debian12:nonroot, tag + digest Post-exploitation tooling: no shell, package manager or compiler Vulnerable code in the binary itself No shell means no docker exec sh; debug with an ephemeral debug container or a separate debug image
    User root (uid 0) 65532:65532 Writing root-owned files, binding <1024 without caps Kernel bugs reachable by unprivileged users Bind-mounted volumes must be writable by that uid; fails at start, visibly
    Capabilities 40 effective (privileged) cap_drop: ALL, CapEff=0 chown, mknod, raw sockets, mount via CAP_* checks Anything that needs no capability Needs NET_BIND_SERVICE for port 80/443 unless you remap ports; ping needs NET_RAW
    no-new-privileges NoNewPrivs: 0 NoNewPrivs: 1 setuid/file-capability privilege gain on execve A process that is already privileged Breaks legitimate setuid helpers (sudo, ping on some images)
    Seccomp none (Seccomp: 0) allowlist, default ERRNO Namespace creation via clone, mount, ptrace, bpf, module loading, open_by_handle_at Abuse of syscalls that remain allowed Highest false-positive risk of any control here; see Seccomp profile
    Root filesystem writable read_only: true + 8 MiB noexec tmpfs on /tmp Persisting a payload or tampering with binaries in the image layer Memory-only attacks; writes to any mounted volume Every writable path must be enumerated; apps that write to /var/cache break at runtime
    Resource limits none 128 MiB (no swap), 64 PIDs, 0.5 CPU Memory exhaustion, fork exhaustion, CPU starvation of neighbours Network or disk-bandwidth exhaustion An undersized limit is an availability incident, not a security event; size from measured peaks
    Namespaces pid: host own PID namespace Enumerating and signalling host processes — None for this app
    Socket / mounts Docker socket, writable host dir none Daemon API access (host-root equivalent), host file tampering — CI runners and reverse proxies often want the socket; give them a socket proxy or a rootless daemon instead
    Network default bridge, 0.0.0.0:8080 internal: true, no published port Egress to anything outside the network; reachability of the canary Abuse of what the app is allowed to talk to An internal-only service needs a second hop for ingress (a proxy on both networks)
    Supply chain unpinned tag, no signature digest pins, SBOM, cosign signature + attestation Tag substitution; unverified bytes A compromised build pipeline that signs bad bytes Digest pins stop receiving base-image fixes until bumped (observed below)

    Seccomp profile¶

    I did not copy a profile. scripts/gen-seccomp.sh extracts /app/posture from the built image, runs it under strace -f for the service workload and the lab-harness subcommands, removes a fixed deny list the probe attempts on purpose (strace records an attempt even when the kernel refuses it, so without this step the profile would learn the attacks), and emits a default-ERRNO allowlist. Observed on this run:

    service syscalls allowed : 41
runtime hand-off allowed : 3  ['fstatfs', 'statfs', 'statx']
harness-only allowed     : 9  ['dup3', 'mkdirat', 'newfstatat', 'pidfd_open', 'pidfd_send_signal', 'pipe2', 'readlinkat', 'unlinkat', 'waitid']
observed but removed     : 4  ['fchownat', 'mknodat', 'mount', 'umount2']

    Status: tested locally. The output above is from the run that generated the committed hardened/seccomp.json.

    Three things I learned the hard way, all observed:

    1. An application trace is not enough. The first profile left the container unable to start: runc init itself issues syscalls after the filter is loaded and before execve. On runc 1.5.2 the failure walked from fstatfs to statx before the container came up. That "hand-off" set is runtime-version dependent; re-derive it when runc changes.
    2. clone needs an argument filter, not an allow. The profile allows clone only when flags & 0x7E020000 == 0 (the namespace flags) and returns ENOSYS for clone3, because seccomp cannot inspect the clone3 flags struct and libc/Go fall back to clone. This matches the structure of Moby's default profile (source-reviewed: moby/profiles seccomp/default.json, which uses the same 2114060288 mask and errnoRet: 38 for clone3 when CAP_SYS_ADMIN is absent).
    3. A denial is only evidence if you know which layer produced it. mount, chown, mknod and raw sockets are refused by capability checks as well, so they cannot show that seccomp works. User-namespace creation through clone(CLONE_NEWUSER) needs no capability (Docker's seccomp documentation calls this out), so it is the discriminating probe. I also tried unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER) first and got EINVAL even with every restriction off (tested locally). unshare(2) documents EINVAL for CLONE_NEWUSER when the caller is multithreaded (source-reviewed), and a Go program is always multithreaded. A probe that fails for an unrelated reason would have looked like a pass.

    The default action is ERRNO, not KILL. A missed syscall then degrades one request instead of killing PID 1 and restart-looping the service. The cost is that a blocked syscall can be swallowed by code that ignores errors.

    Image scanning: what the numbers say, and what they do not¶

    This is where my expectation was wrong, so I am recording it as found. tested locally, Trivy 0.76.1, vulnerability DB updated 2026-11-04 19:02 UTC, both images built from golang:1.27-alpine (Go 1.27.3):

    Measure insecure (alpine 3.24.3 + toolchain) hardened (debian 12.15 distroless)
    Unique CVE/package findings 0 4 (all UNKNOWN severity: Debian LTS advisories against ca-certificates and tzdata; fixed versions exist)
    SBOM-only scan (trivy sbom on the Syft CycloneDX file) 0 4 (agrees with the image scan)
    SBOM components by type 39 library, 213 file, 1 application, 1 OS 7 library, 950 file, 1 OS
    Executable files in the image 86 10
    Shell / package manager / compiler ash+sh / apk / go none / none / none
    Image content size 356,984,047 bytes 9,404,585 bytes

    Reading it correctly:

    • A CVE count did not rank these images by risk. The image with a shell, a package manager and a compiler had no known vulnerabilities on the day it was scanned; the hardened image had four. The hardened image's attack surface is far smaller, which is why the lab measures it directly (tests/inventory.py walks the exported filesystem) instead of trusting scan counts.
    • The hardened image is older on purpose, and that is a trade. Pinning the distroless base by digest makes the build reproducible and stops a registry-side tag move from changing what you run. It also freezes the base at the digest I pinned, so Debian updates that landed afterwards show up as findings. Digest pinning only works with automation that bumps the digest (Renovate/Dependabot or a scheduled rebuild) and re-scans. I did not build that automation here.
    • Raw counts mislead; deduplicate. An earlier scan of the same two images built from golang:1.24-alpine reported 976 raw findings for the insecure image, which collapse to 116 unique CVE/package pairs because the same Go standard-library CVEs repeat for every Go binary in the toolchain. The hardened image, then, carried 23 HIGH findings from the toolchain's standard library. Those two scans are kept as a clearly-labeled one-off record, observation-go124-toolchain-scan.json, and cannot be regenerated: the images no longer exist and the DB moves daily. Moving the builder to a supported toolchain removed them. The lesson is that "distroless" does not mean "no findings": a statically linked Go binary carries its toolchain's standard library.
    • SBOM totals are not comparable. 958 vs 254 components looks like the opposite of the truth; file-level components (every zoneinfo file in tzdata) dominate. Compare package-level components.
    • Trivy's Dockerfile checks agreed with my gate on the big items. It flagged the insecure Dockerfile for root user (DS-0002, HIGH), no HEALTHCHECK (DS-0026) and the secret-shaped ENV (DS-0031, CRITICAL) and reported nothing for the hardened one. My gate reports 30 findings vs 0 because it also covers Compose.

    Signing: what local-only signing proves¶

    scripts/sign-verify.sh runs a registry:2 container on loopback, generates an ephemeral key pair with a random one-time password (never written to disk or committed), and signs with an empty signing config (no Fulcio, Rekor or TSA). cosign v3 deprecates --tlog-upload=false; an explicit empty signing config is the supported way to say "no transparency service". Results (tested locally, evidence/signing__summary.json):

    Case Expected Observed
    Verify the signed hardened digest, right key accept accepted
    Verify the unsigned insecure digest reject rejected (no signatures found)
    Verify the signed digest with an unrelated key reject rejected
    Verify by tag, then re-point the tag at different content and verify again accept, then reject accepted, then rejected
    Verify the SBOM attestation (cyclonedx) accept accepted
    Verify the same digest as slsaprovenance reject rejected

    This proves the mechanics: a signature binds to a digest, so tag substitution fails verification. It does not prove: who signed (the key is anonymous), when (no transparency log or timestamp), or that the signer was your pipeline. Production needs keyless signing bound to a CI workload identity or a KMS/HSM key, a transparency log, and verification at admission against a pinned identity. The existing Kubernetes lab contains the admission-side ImageValidatingPolicy and its offline model; neither is exercised against a real signature here.

    Validation¶

    All commands run from the repository root. Environment for the recorded run (evidence/versions.txt): Linux kernel 6.18.44, Docker Engine 29.9.2 (overlayfs snapshotter, cgroup v1), Compose 5.6.1, runc 1.5.2, Trivy 0.76.1, Syft 1.56.0, cosign v3.1.4, strace 6.8. docker info listed only seccomp under security options.

    node --test labs/docker-security/tests/policy-check.test.js     # no Docker needed
bash labs/docker-security/scripts/run-lab.sh --publish-evidence  # needs a disposable Docker host

    Static gate (tested locally, no Docker)¶

    node labs/docker-security/tests/policy-check.js labs/docker-security/insecure → 30 findings, exit 1. ... hardened → 0 findings, exit 0. 38 unit tests pass: one positive and one negative case per rule, plus the cases below. Writing them found a real defect in my own rule: docker.sock:ro evaded the socket rule because the regex anchored on end-of-string. A read-only mount of a socket file does not restrict API calls, so the rule now matches :ro, containerd.sock, podman.sock and crio.sock as well.

    Runtime comparison (tested locally)¶

    Observed from inside the running service containers via docker compose exec ... probe (evidence/runtime__*-probe.json):

    Observation Insecure Hardened
    Effective uid 0 65532
    CapEff 000001fffeffffff (40 capabilities, no SYS_RESOURCE because this VM drops it) 0000000000000000
    NoNewPrivs / Seccomp 0 / 0 (off) 1 / 2 (filter, 1 filter)
    Root filesystem writable read-only
    Memory / PIDs / CPU unlimited / unlimited / unlimited 134217728 / 64 / 50000 µs per 100000
    Visible processes, PID 1 96, the VM's init (host PID namespace) 2, posture
    write_root_filesystem allowed EROFS
    write_tmp_scratch allowed allowed (the app still works)
    chown_to_other_uid, mknod_char_device, raw_socket, mount_tmpfs allowed EPERM each
    clone_new_user_namespace allowed EPERM
    Docker socket present, GET /_ping → HTTP/1.0 200 OK ENOENT
    Bind-mounted host directory read and write allowed; file written by the container is owned by uid 0 on the host ENOENT
    TCP to the canary service allowed blocked, name does not resolve (different network)

    Seccomp attribution controls (same user, caps dropped, no-new-privileges, read-only; only --security-opt seccomp varies, evidence/runtime__hardened-seccomp-*-probe.json):

    seccomp setting Seccomp mode clone(CLONE_NEWUSER)
    unconfined 0 allowed
    Docker default profile 2 EPERM
    this lab's derived profile 2 EPERM

    With capabilities already empty, the only thing that changes between rows is the seccomp setting. That is what makes the denial attributable to the filter.

    Resource limits:

    Test Insecure Hardened
    forktest 200 (bounded: sleeping children, then exit) 200 started 13 started, EAGAIN (Go runtime threads count against the 64-PID limit)
    memtest 512 (touch 512 MiB) exit 0 killed, exit 137; last progress line touched_mib: 112

    After the hardened OOM kill, Docker reported running oom_killed=true health=healthy. The kernel killed the exec'd test process, not PID 1, so the service stayed up. That is OOM victim selection, not a guarantee: a leak in the service itself would be the victim, and Docker's own documentation notes the kernel kills processes in a container when it hits its limit. Treat limits as availability controls.

    What the lab asserts¶

    run-lab.sh ends by running tests/runtime_check.py, which exits nonzero when any observed value differs from the claims above: 85 passed, 0 failed on the recorded run. Supply-chain assertions print SKIP with the recorded reason when Trivy, Syft or cosign are absent, never a silent pass.

    What was not tested¶

    • AppArmor / SELinux profiles. docker info showed name=seccomp only; /sys/kernel/security/lsm does not exist on this VM kernel, so no LSM profile could be loaded. Not executed. Docker's security documentation describes AppArmor and SELinux as an additional layer; whatever a production host adds on top of the controls measured here is unmeasured.
    • Rootless Docker and userns-remap. Not executed. These change what "uid 0 in the container" means and are the control I would add for workloads that must run as root.
    • cgroup v2. The run was on cgroup v1. The probe reads both layouts, but the v2 paths were not exercised.
    • Windows, macOS/Docker Desktop, Podman, containerd-direct.
    • Hosted CI. run-lab.sh is not part of npm run verify:native-labs; adding a privileged-container job to the gating workflow without a hosted-runner trial would risk blocking publication. Static tests are in npm run validate.
    • Keyless signing, Rekor, a transparency-log-backed verification, KMS keys. Local ephemeral key only.
    • Runtime detection (Falco, Tetragon, auditd) for the behaviours the probe exercises. See the Linux telemetry lab for synthetic detection logic.
    • Escape techniques. The lab does not attempt container escapes, and a passing run is not a claim that none exist.
    • Reproducible builds. The two images rebuild with different digests each time; -trimpath and a pinned builder narrow the gap but I did not verify bit-for-bit reproducibility.

    Production considerations¶

    Rollout. Do not enable everything at once. Order by blast radius and ease of rollback: (1) digest pins and non-root, (2) no-new-privileges and cap_drop: ALL with a measured add-back list, (3) read-only root with a tmpfs inventory, (4) resource limits from observed peaks plus headroom, (5) seccomp last, in a lower environment first. For seccomp, ship SCMP_ACT_LOG (needs auditd/journald) for at least one full release cycle and review the denied syscalls before switching to ERRNO; this lab went straight to ERRNO because its workload is fully enumerated.

    False positives. The things that break first are exactly the things hardening removes: apps that write outside declared paths (EROFS), images that expect root-owned volumes (EACCES), services that silently ignore EPERM from a blocked syscall, setuid helpers, JIT runtimes and anything calling clone3. A seccomp profile learned from a bounded workload will miss rare paths (a reload handler, a crash dumper, a TLS renegotiation path); mitigate with staged LOG mode, a regression test that exercises every code path, and a per-service exception process.

    Detection. Alert on the configuration, not only the behaviour: privileged, cap_add, docker.sock mounts, pid: host, seccomp=unconfined and writable host bind mounts at CI/admission time (this lab's gate is a starting point). At runtime, a container that performs mount, namespace creation or writes to a read-only path is a signal only if you collect the denial; EPERM from seccomp is silent unless you configure logging. I did not test a runtime sensor.

    Operability. Debugging a shell-less image needs a documented procedure (ephemeral debug container sharing the PID namespace, or a debug tag of the image that is never deployed to production). Health checks must not assume curl. Exit 137 after a limit change is the OOM killer, not a crash loop. Track image age: a digest-pinned base that nobody bumps becomes the scan finding you are paying to avoid.

    Blast radius. Even fully hardened, containers share the host kernel. The controls here shrink reachable kernel surface and what an attacker can do post-exploit; they do not make this safe for hostile multi-tenant code. For that, add a user-namespaced or VM-isolated runtime (gVisor, Kata, Firecracker) and say so in the threat model.

    Rollback. Everything is declarative: revert the image digest or the Compose file. Keep the previous profile versioned beside the image tag. The break-glass setting seccomp=unconfined is dangerous precisely because it works; make it a time-boxed exception that alerts, never a default fix for a failing deploy.

    Reproduce¶

    Prerequisites: Docker Engine with Compose v2, Node.js 22+ (npm ci --ignore-scripts for the yaml dependency), Python 3. Optional, each recorded as not executed when absent: trivy, syft, cosign (versions above), and strace only to regenerate the profile.

    npm ci --ignore-scripts
node --test labs/docker-security/tests/policy-check.test.js
bash labs/docker-security/scripts/run-lab.sh                      # raw output in .artifacts/research/docker-security/
bash labs/docker-security/scripts/gen-seccomp.sh                  # optional: regenerate hardened/seccomp.json

    Expect Trivy results to differ from the table above: the vulnerability database changes daily, and Docker Hub may rate-limit base-image pulls (I hit HTTP 429 once during development; a retry succeeded).

    Teardown. run-lab.sh removes both stacks, the registry container, the canary directory and its temp key material on exit. Images (dockerlab/posture:*) and the base-image cache remain; remove them with docker image rm.
